title: Whole-graph profile-guided WinUI release comparison
rustc:
rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28)
binary: rustc
commit-hash: b940084d7eb6a299eb4bfeb8e34901bc051e7ac4
commit-date: 2026-09-28
host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
release: 1.99.0
LLVM version: 23.1.1

arms.main_shipping: The property-only fixture built against original main with its release ThinLTO settings.
arms.final_fat: Merged runtime, compact FatLTO s, unprofiled. The application startup and memory tables call this same arm selected_fat.
arms.final_pgo: Merged runtime, compact FatLTO using the profile and opt level identified by its parent cohort. The application tables call this arm pgo.

required_tools: Rust with matching LLVM llvm-profdata, LLD and a GNU/Linux x86-64 runtime with DT_RELR support
recipe.scope: This recipe regenerates the training data and stripped shipping executables. Host tools and proc macros are built separately from the explicitly targeted instrumented dependencies.

use.target_opt_level: s or z, for every target dependency and final crate

scenarios: Button, NavigationView and ScrollViewer template activation
training.coverage_method: Count unique covered Rust v0 definitions by the first crate root in each symbol from llvm-profdata show --all-functions --counts --covered.

profile_use_evidence.method: Matching LLVM opt -passes=print-profile-summary on the first object module of each named target rlib before final FatLTO. Counts are per sampled module.

profile_hash_mismatches.source: Cargo profile-use build diagnostics, including any replayed dependency diagnostics. One row per reported function control-flow hash mismatch.

build_cost.scope: The profiled dependency artifacts were already staged. This is the dependency-warm shipping Cargo build including the final FatLTO compile and link.

archive_checks.typed_values: Normal and compact ControlContentThemeFontSize values read by the shipping probe.

public_property_tests.method: Public Base property tests linked against the same profile-use Base rlib with the final property fixture flags, then run serially.

startup.condition: 81 rotating fresh warm processes to typed Button; 31 additional processes per binary after verified executable-page eviction. Same CPU for all participants.
startup.end_point: spawn through the first verified typed Button resource. Rendering and first paint were not measured.

resident.workload: Complete process lifetime including theme teardown after first verified typed Button lookup. Linux wait4, warm filesystem.

method.workload: 11 public i32 property operations on four concrete host types, panic=unwind
method.design: Every 24 measured blocks exercise all permutations of four arms in seeded shuffled order. Each permutation is followed immediately by its reverse, with the same workload rotation for all eight fresh processes. The three initial warmup blocks are retained separately and excluded from statistics.
method.confidence: 95% percentile bootstrap (4000 resamples) of the median within-block CPU ratio. Each arm contributes its mean of two CPU ns/op observations in that block.
method.training_overlap: The trainer exercised these same eleven public operations. Measurement uses separately linked fixtures and fresh processes. These results characterize this workload distribution.

public_property_cpu.layout: Blocks are in collection order and include the initial warmups. Each row starts with the arm and gives one process's total thread CPU nanoseconds for each lane in workload_order. Divide by that lane's operation count. Each arm occurs twice per block.

profile_use_evidence.method: Matching LLVM opt -passes=print-profile-summary on the first object module of each named target rlib before final FatLTO. Counts are per sampled module.

profile_hash_mismatches.source: Cargo profile-use build diagnostics, including any replayed dependency diagnostics. One row per reported function control-flow hash mismatch.

build_cost.scope: Cargo profile-use target build at z, including changed target dependencies and the final FatLTO compile and link. The elapsed time is not directly comparable with the dependency-warm s measurement.
